description: Sanitized real llama-fit-params outputs for Phase 4b probe-parser and Phase 4c fit-search tests. Covers both backend output shapes (Metal with dedicated CPU_REPACK row, CUDA with host-model-column growth), the unit-step points around the 16 GiB placement boundary (ADR section 13), the dense-model architecture-agnostic check, and one parse-failure sample.
captured_with: llama-fit-params --fit off -fitp on -lm none -lv 4 (plus per-fixture flags)

sources.ryne: RTX 5090 32GB (CUDA), remote Windows host over SSH

invariants_confirmed: 464 MiB per offloaded MoE layer, constant across both platforms (model-determined, not platform-determined)
Metal: device model column falls per layer; a stderr-only CPU_REPACK row rises by the same amount; Host model column stays flat
CUDA: device model column falls per layer; no CPU_REPACK row; Host model column carries the growth instead
Enabling offload (n=0->4 step) carries a one-time transition cost on top of the per-layer cost (98 MiB excess on first CUDA step)
ubatch is a real but second-order device lever: ~471 MiB device delta across ub 256->1024 (~one offloaded layer)
KV footprint is an architecture property, not a per-parameter rule of thumb: dense 27B context=6796 MiB vs MoE 35B context=2140 MiB at identical -c and K/V quant
16 GiB placement boundary lands between surveyed multiples of 4 (n=16 and n=20), first satisfied at n=18 -- unit-step fixtures are required, coarse survey points are not enough

The probe binary only rejects negative --n-cpu-moe values itself (CLI usage error, exit!=0); over-limit and dense-model+n-cpu-moe cases are silently accepted/ignored by the binary and MUST be rejected at the Rust preset-validation layer instead
